items.label: About 35% censored (Methods text)

assumptions.what: Binary covariates X5 to X7 are the multivariate normal draw cut at 0.5, as the text says; this weakens their correlation with the other covariates (X1 with X6: 0.77 in the data, 0.61 generated)
assumptions.sensitivity: Keeping the observed correlations moves the empirical SE of X1 from 0.0051 to 0.0064 and of X6 from 0.104 to 0.132 (paper 0.0060 and 0.119); see truth_variants.json

assumptions.what: Hazards are per day, 2-year survival at 730.5 days, predicted at the means of all covariates
assumptions.sensitivity: The full-data 2-year survival is 0.776 against the figure's 0.78

cause.summary: The text's 'approximately 35%' is a rounded figure: the stated hazards (0.0002 for censoring against 0.00027 exp(LP) for events) give 36.4% censored in our run and 36.6% with every variant of our generator.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our binary covariates or the floor at 0 change the censoring
hypotheses.test: Censored share of 20,000 cohorts under each generator variant (truth_variants.json)

hypotheses.hypothesis: The stated hazards give about 36%, which the text rounds to 35
hypotheses.test: Every variant gives 36.6% (2000 cohorts each) and our 200 replicates 36.4%

items.label: Missingness design: incomplete cases, shares and overlaps (Methods text)

assumptions.what: Missingness intercepts solved at the average value of each mechanism's term; continuous terms (and survival time, as log(t / SD(t))) divided by their SD
assumptions.sensitivity: Realised shares in text.design

cause.summary: Each covariate is missing in exactly its share of all cases (X3 at 25%: 67.98% of 25.75% incomplete cases is 17.50% of all cases, the design's 0.70 x 25%), but the overall share of incomplete cases runs 0.3 to 0.8 points above the target because only three pairs of indicators are tied (X5 and X3 or X8 and X2 can be missing together by chance). The shares of incomplete cases then fall slightly below the stated ones. The paper's numbers are design targets ('approximately'), and how it tied the other pairs is not stated.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The per-covariate rates are wrong
hypotheses.test: Share of incomplete cases times the incomplete rate against the design's share times the level, every level (comparison.json)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Untied pairs of indicators add incomplete cases
hypotheses.test: The excess of incomplete cases over the target (0.3 to 0.8 points) against the chance overlap of X5 with X3 and of X8 with X2 under independence

cause.summary: Our generator's empirical SEs are 14% smaller for X1 and X6 and 14% larger for X4 than the paper's, and its true values 1 to 5% larger in magnitude for X2, X3, X4 and X5 (X7 0.8%). Keeping the binaries' observed correlations takes the X1 and X6 SEs past the paper's (0.0064 and 0.132 against 0.0060 and 0.119, ours 0.0051 and 0.104); the unrounded coefficients move X2's true value from 0.0517 to 0.0513 (paper 0.0507); the X4 SE and the larger magnitudes stay open.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The binary covariates of the paper kept their observed correlations (the 0.5 cut-point weakens X1 with X6 from 0.77 to 0.61)
hypotheses.test: True-value cohorts with the binaries' covariances divided by the attenuation of the cut (truth_variants.json, 2000 cohorts)

hypotheses.test: True-value cohorts with GBSG2's unrounded coefficients (truth_variants.json)

cause.summary: Most points fall within Monte Carlo error. Most of the 32 misses are estimates of X2, X3, X4 and X5 at 50 and 75% (five at 25%), mostly MI and SI, where our MIX without truncating, MICE-PMM and SI are further from or nearer the truth than the paper's. The offset of the true values does not explain them; the 2004 to 2005 package versions could not be tested.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The offset between our true values and the paper's explains the misses
hypotheses.test: Compare each point's bias from its own run's true value instead of its value (comparison.json, bias_relative_to_own_truth)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Monte Carlo error at 200 replicates
hypotheses.test: Tolerance of three combined Monte Carlo SEs; at that tolerance chance alone misses about 1 point in 370, and the misses cluster in a few covariates and methods instead of spreading

hypotheses.hypothesis: The imputation packages changed since 2004 to 2005 (mice 1.13.1, Hmisc 2.2-3, norm 1.0-9, mix 1.0-4 against mice 3.16.0, Hmisc 5.1-1, norm 1.0-11.1, mix 1.0-13), and with them the defaults the paper does not state

hypotheses.hypothesis: Another standard rule for combining the m = 20 analyses gives the paper's p-values
hypotheses.test: 152 replicates at 50 and 75% MAR, five MI methods, each pooled with D1 (Wald, Rubin's rules), a Wald test on the total variance, D2 (Li et al. 1991, the paper's stated method), D2 on var(d), D3 (Meng and Rubin 1992) and the mean, median and maximum of the m p-values (pipeline/pooling_check.R, output/pooling_check.csv; D2 equals the committed run in all 1,520 rows). At 75% the mean p stays at 10^-17 to 10^-6 for every rule except D3 with MIX without truncating (0.05, from single replicates near 1), against the paper's 4.7 x 10^-4 to 4.6 x 10^-3; the largest single replicate with D2 is 4 x 10^-4
